text:
morgan.infra: Quick heads up — we're doing a preemptive node quarantine in us-east1-gpu-pool tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. Scope: NIC firmware + minor host kernel micropatch across 6 racks. This will be a rolling quarantine (small cohorts) not a full drain. Expect ~5% effective GPU capacity hit during the window. We'll route traffic to burst pools and prefer dedicated customers for least disruption.

jess.product: Which SKU/pools are in the cohort? Any customer-facing notices planned? :thinking_face:

morgan.infra: Cohorts are: pool-us-east1-gpu-a (primary), pool-us-east1-gpu-b (secondary warm), and 2 racks in pool-us-east1-edge. We'll mark routes with `maintenance=us-east1-q1` so console and billing can tag. I'll open an internal notice and coord with comms.

samir.oncall: Please add an autoscaler exception — scaling down during the window will be disabled for these pools. Also add p95 latency watch on the hosted API. If we see tail latency >150ms we start rollback.

morgan.infra: Yep adding exception. Rollback policy: if API p95 > 150ms for 10m OR embedding request errors >0.5% over 5m, abort and backfill with cross-region capacity.

alex.sre: Quick ask — can we avoid KV-cache invalidation on the warmback? Last time TTL reset spiked token costs. Maybe keep cache shards pinned to cohort IDs.

morgan.infra: Good call. Plan is to keep prefix/KV caches warm by scheduling a low-traffic warmup (500 req/min) to each replaced host right after rejoin. No global TTL reset.

infra-bot: maintenance-ticket #INF-2248 created by morgan.infra — runbook attached. Link: https://redwood-infra/ops/INF-2248

jess.product: Should we proactively message high-usage customers in us-east? Might save support load.

morgan.infra: Yes — sending a 1-paragraph heads-up to customers with >200k tokens/day in that region. Also enabling soft-throttle protections for system tests to avoid noisy-neighbor flares.

samir.oncall: Command we will use for graceful cordon/drain (cohort size = 6 nodes at a time):

```
kubectl cordon node-xyz && kubectl drain node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m
```

samir.oncall: Note — don't run `--force`; we want pods to respect preStop hooks.

morgan.infra: Backfill plan: 1) enable burst pool routing, 2) spin 12 small spot GPUs in us-west as temporary extra capacity (auto-deprovision on finish), 3) increase request batching thresholds slightly to reduce per-token load. Cost impact estimated ~+$2.3k for the window.

alex.sre: Can we set transient budget cap so cost owners get alerted?

morgan.infra: Yes — adding an alert to billing-alerts (threshold +20% over baseline for that pool).

jess.product: SGTM. Any known networking risk? Last NIC patch caused one rack to reboot twice.

morgan.infra: We've staged firmware version this week on a single test rack (no regressions). For safety we have a two-pass approach: patch + 30m soak, then host kernel micropatch + 45m soak. If a node reboots twice within 30m, it gets fenced and pulled out of rotation for manual debug.

samir.oncall: Please tag the runbook with the oncall play: `pgw-fence` and ensure PagerDuty escalation is a single alert for the cohort.

infrastructure: will kick off smoke tests after each cohort: perf-check (p50/p95), correctness-eval (sample prompts), and embedding-consistency.

morgan.infra: I'll post the full timeline and the runbook link in #incidents 1h before start. If anyone wants to be in the Zoom runbook room, ping me and I'll add. :thumbsup:

jess.product: Thanks — appreciate the heads up.

samir.oncall: Oncall will monitor from 01:30 UTC and stand ready to roll back.

morgan.infra: Final note: this is maintenance-only; no config changes to model routing or billing. All changes are orchestration-level and reversible.
